answer: A fresh identity has no pulse of sealed grading work behind it. On PoA a key earns standing only by submitting quorum-reaching grades epoch after epoch, each an on-chain tx that bumps a monotone nonce — a ledger you cannot buy or hand over. Like a willow, trust grows slow and deep-rooted; a sparrow-light clone that only just registered has none. To fake N trusted identities an attacker must actually perform N times the grading labor across many epochs, so cost scales linearly with the number of fakes and never amortizes into one warmed credential.
